audit.why: 54.62% over 4603 games with a TRICKY 7/10 label. The lane is genuinely split: Yasuo owns the early dash-and-wall window, Fizz owns the burst windows after 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers of the level chart disagree on six of seven rows. Content win[] reads Fizz/Yasuo/Yasuo/Skill/Fizz/Fizz/Fizz and the packet levelChart is identical; full phases[].side reads Yasuo/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Yasuo. Every phases[].why is also the stock Fizz-wins string regardless of which side the row gives the stage to. whys[5] and whys[6] are swapped across the First item and 2+ items rows.
audit.why: Content and packet agree exactly, so the full layer is the lone outlier and is brought to them. Grounding for the shape: Steel Tempest is a flat 4s and needs two stacks to knock up, so level 1 is not his; Sweeping Blade is 0.5s at rank 1 off any minion, so levels 2-3 are; Fizz's shark and first item put the burst windows back to Fizz.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side=Fizz, [1]=Yasuo, [2]=Yasuo, [4]=Fizz, [5]=Fizz, [6]=Fizz, with ratings and every why rewritten to argue the same verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this matchup is stated wrongly in five places. The page says Wind Wall blocks 'Seastone Trident and Nomadic Squirtle' (wants.foe[0], spikes[0]) and 'your E slow and R splash' (early). Nomadic Squirtle is not a Fizz ability at all. Seastone Trident is Fizz's W, an on-hit bleed on melee autos, and Playful/Trickster is a hop — neither is a projectile. The only Fizz ability Wind Wall blocks is Chum the Waters (R). whys[4] and wants.you[2] additionally claim the ult can be angled 'around' the wall.
audit.why: Kit flags: Fizz R is the sole ability flagged projectile; Fizz Q and E are dashes, W is an auto-attack effect. Yasuo W is flagged blocksProjectiles and terrain, 25/23/21/19/17s, 4 seconds' duration. So the real rule is simple and the page never states it: your dash-in and your pole go through the wall; the fish does not.
audit.corrected: Every mention corrected to Chum the Waters, with the positive half — Q and E ignore the wall — stated so the reader knows what still works.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns has no digit in it (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and Wind Wall's cooldown is the number the whole matchup is scheduled around.
audit.why: Wind Wall 25s at rank 1 down to 17s at rank 5, up for 4 seconds; Steel Tempest a flat 4s; Last Breath 70/50/30s and requires an Airborne target.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warns that fighting next to your own team's CC hands Yasuo a Last Breath reset, despite the kit making it explicit.
audit.why: Last Breath blinks to any Airborne enemy champion and is only 30s at rank 3.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.late, breakdown.carry and whys[6].

Once you hit 6, Playful/Trickster lets you find engage angles his Wind Wall can't fully block, especially if you bait the wall out first with a fake approach or wave clear. This swings the all-in window back in your favour, so look to punish him whenever his wall and dash are both down.

That swings the all-in window back to you whenever wall and dash are down.

CHART: the full layer disagreed with the content layer on six of seven rows. Content win[] and the packet levelChart are identical to each other, so I moved the full-layer sides onto the content values rather than the reverse; consequently these side edits carry no paired win[N] edit, because win[N] already holds the target value on disk and an edit with a matching before/after would be a no-op. The whys were rewritten in the same proposal so no row argues against its own verdict. 'Nomadic Squirtle' is a fabricated Fizz ability name and was removed from wants.foe[0] and spikes[0]. Wind Wall's real reach in this matchup is Chum the Waters only — Seastone Trident is an on-hit effect on melee autos and Playful/Trickster is a hop, neither of which is a projectile. Whether Yasuo's Wind Wall blocks the shark's eruption after the fish has already attached is not answerable from Riot's text and I did not assert it.
